e5d137ab-5b82-4ba1-9d67-9bdedc7d6fb6.job_description:
You will develop and integrate real-time vision algorithms that operate under strict latency and compute constraints. This includes detecting and tracking objects and people from live video streams, estimating scene geometry from monocular and sensor-fused inputs, and building spatial understanding systems that support autonomous navigation decisions.

On the autonomy side, you will work on closed-loop systems - position stabilisation, obstacle avoidance, and path planning in GPS-denied indoor environments with outputs connected directly to embedded control hardware. The focus throughout is on making these systems reliable in real-world operation, not just in simulation or notebooks.



Skills You Need to Have
Strong Python with real threading and performance awareness
OpenCV beyond tutorials - optical flow, feature matching, camera geometry, calibration
PyTorch for inference deployment - fp16, ONNX, optimisation, not just training
Solid 3D geometry - camera intrinsics, rigid transforms, reprojection, coordinate frames
Real-time systems mindset - latency budgets, profiling, pipeline bottlenecks


Skills That Will Set You Apart
Hands-on experience deploying detection or tracking models at live framerates
Familiarity with depth estimation, visual odometry, or SLAM in any form
Exposure to edge compute - Jetson, Raspberry Pi, or similar constrained hardware
Any experience with robotics communication protocols and embedded control systems
Prior work involving real hardware, sensor integration, or field testing


Who Should Apply
Final-year students or recent graduates in CS / AI / ECE / Robotics or related disciplines
Candidates with demonstrable project work - not just coursework
People comfortable with systems that move, fail, and need to be debugged in the real world
